title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
prompt: Given an array of integers `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting and ending index of a given `target` value. If `target` is not found, return `[-1, -1]`. Your algorithm must run in `O(log n)` time.
hints: Once you find any occurrence of target with a normal binary search, expanding outward linearly to find the bounds costs O(n) in the worst case (e.g. all elements equal target).
Instead run two separate binary searches: one biased to find the leftmost index where target could be inserted, another biased to find the leftmost index where target + 1 could be inserted.
The first search's result is the start of target's range (if it actually equals target); the second search's result minus one is the end of that range.

solution.approach: Run a 'find leftmost insertion point' binary search twice: once for target itself to get the start of its range, and once for target + 1 to get one past the end of its range. Both searches are the same lower-bound binary search, just parameterized by a different value, so they run in O(log n) each. If the start index is out of bounds or nums[start] isn't actually target, the value doesn't exist and the answer is [-1, -1]; otherwise the range is [start, end - 1].
